query: Consider the following context: How to rationally design composition of alloys with desired properties has always been an open and challenging question, especially for high-entropy alloy (HEA) which has huge selections of composition due to the feature of multi-principal elements. Although great efforts have been made in the past decades, such as approaches based on thermo-kinetic analysis and simulations, strategies to quick determine the optimal HEA composition remain lacking. In that context, which method can be used for design intrinsically strong, ductile, and low-weight refractory HEA (RHEA) compositions, and why?

generation.hypothesis: A machine learning-based computational method can be used to design intrinsically strong, ductile, and low-weight refractory HEA (RHEA) compositions by predicting optimal composition based on thermodynamic and kinetic principles.
generation.material_initial_state: Multi-principal elements with huge selections of composition
generation.intervention: Machine learning-based computational method to predict optimal composition
generation.predicted_outcome: 20% increase in strength, 15% increase in ductility, and 10% decrease in weight compared to baseline RHEA compositions
generation.boundary: Composition range limited to refractory elements
generation.uncertainty: The accuracy of the machine learning model may be affected by the quality and quantity of training data, and the complexity of the thermodynamic and kinetic principles involved.

falsification_experiment.design: Comparative study of RHEA compositions designed using machine learning-based computational method and conventional methods
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the machine learning-based computational method does not result in a significant improvement (p < 0.05) in at least two of the measured properties compared to conventional methods, the hypothesis is falsified.
